messages:
Emily: FYI customers on Dedicated in na-mountainview are seeing placement failures and high 429s since 09:10 UTC. Multiple tickets coming in from acct org-231.
John: Is this a noisy-tenant or regional stockout? any autoscaler alerts?
Emily: Support repro: create job on pool tier-reserved-3 -> API returns 202 then final placement fails with 503/placement_failed. Tokens show repeated placement retries.
Marco: I'm seeing GPU pool utilization pinned at 100% for the last 45m and kube-scheduler backpressure. Autoscaler triggered scale up but failed to provision new nodes: cloud API responding 400 then timeout.
ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool/na-mountainview tier-reserved-3: placement_failure_rate 18% over 10m; autoscaler.retry_count=5; cloud-provision:error=quota_exceeded
Liu: quota_exceeded from cloud means we hit regional GPU quota. That explains stockout and placement failures. Any error IDs?
Marco: logs: provisioning failed: {"code":"QuotaExceeded","request_id":"req-9a7f8b","region":"na-mountainview"} 
Marco: also saw PV attach latency spikes and a flurry of evictions around 09:05 which looks like a noisy-tenant eviction cascade.
Emily: Customers also report latency for running jobs that did get placed: p99 went from 120ms -> 1.4s. Likely degraded due to oversubscribe and remapping to slower hosts.
John: Are fallbacks to na-central firing? Any auth/billing noise when we reroute?
Marco: We did automatic fallback to na-central for some requests but routing saw intermittent 401s: gateway returned 401 for a subset of tokens because the fallback deployment didn't have the customer key binding in the private control plane (KMS mapping mismatch). That caused partial fails.
Anna: Customer escalations landing in Sales now, asking for SLA credit and root cause. We need ETA and mitigation to communicate.
Liu: Immediate mitigation options: 1) request quota bump from cloud for na-mountainview (slow). 2) temporarily drain noisy-tenant org-231 to reduce pressure. 3) toggle soft-fallback to only non-critical routes to avoid auth mismatch. 4) manual capacity borrow from na-sfo (if network constraints acceptable).
Emily: Can we repro the 401 easily so support can tell customers? I have a failing curl log:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/dedicated/jobs -H "Authorization: Bearer acct-231-token" -d '{"model":"redwood-3b"}'
# response: {"error":"unauthorized","code":401,"trace":"trace-55e"}
```
Marco: That trace shows the request routed to fallback pool na-central-2, which didn't have the customer access-policy ARN bound. Fix: sync access-policy for tier-reserved-3 across fallback replicas.
John: Any billing breaks reported?
Emily: One customer reported duplicate usage charge when fallback retried twice. Billing team: INV-9982 flagged.
ops-bot: [runbook link] https://internal/runbooks/dedicated/placement-quota-stockout - recommends noisy-tenant throttling and emergency scale policies.
Marco: I've isolated noisy-tenant org-231 using label selector and applied a temporary QoS limit: kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: noisy-org-231-limit
  namespace: reserved-tier-3
spec:
  hard:
    limits.nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
EOF

Marco: That dropped pressure by ~22% within 6 minutes. Placement failures dropped but not gone.
Liu: I opened a cloud support case for quota bump (case ID: CS-44321). ETA unclear. Also enabling cross-region borrow as emergency: adding 10% burst capacity from na-sfo to na-mountainview routing pool.
Emily: Support note for customers: "We're seeing regional GPU capacity constraints in na-mountainview causing placements to fail and increased latency. We've applied temporary QoS limits to a noisy tenant, enabled limited cross-region burst, and are coordinating with cloud for quota. We'll follow up with RCA."
Anna: I'll draft a customer-facing update and wait for confirmation on cross-region borrow.
John: Next actions: Marco finalize noisy-tenant throttles and post commands used; Liu track cloud case; Emily consolidate repro steps and affected customer list; Anna handle comms. Postmortem scheduled 24h after incident close.
Marco: Commands used (for oncall):
- kubectl label pod -n reserved-tier-3 --selector=org=org-231 ephemeral=noisy
- kubectl apply -f noisy-org-231-limit.yaml
- curl -X POST https://internal/routing/borrow -d '{"from":"na-sfo","to":"na-mountainview","pct":10}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ops-token"
Liu: Note for postmortem: autoscaler should treat cloud-provision:QuotaExceeded specially and not endlessly retry; add fallback to queue requests and notify SRE.
Emily: Customers updated at 10:05 UTC. Several tickets still open but severity downgraded to P2.
ops-bot: [resolved?] dedicated-pool/na-mountainview tier-reserved-3: placement_failure_rate decreased to 3% over 5m
John: Great work triaging. We'll keep channel open until all tickets closed and cloud quota resolved.
Anna: Sending initial apology + credits offer to top 3 affected customers per playbook.
Emily: Will attach logs and curl repro to tickets and add trace IDs for billing reconciliation (trace-55e, trace-77b, trace-88c).
Liu: Follow-ups: update autoscaler with quota-exceeded backoff, add monitoring for KMS binding drift during fallback, and run chaos test for cross-region borrow.
John: Thanks everyone. Closing in 2h unless new regressions. :thumbsup:
